settings.help: Turn off to leave Alt+Tab alone, for example if you set your own Alt+Tab bind. Applies after a Hyprland reload.
settings.label: Take over Alt+Tab

settings.help: The key you hold while pressing Tab: Alt (the default), Super or Ctrl. Applies after a Hyprland reload. Super + Tab is Omarchy's next workspace: free it in your bindings first, or omahop leaves it alone and logs why. Omarchy uses Super with most letters, Return and the arrows, so with Super most of the keys that work while the list is up are skipped (a chord you already use is never taken). Ctrl + Tab switches tabs in browsers and editors; with Ctrl it opens omahop instead where omahop is active. The same-app shortcut must start with the same key.
settings.label: Key to hold

settings.help: On other workspaces Alt+Tab stays exactly as Omarchy has it.
settings.label: Where it takes over Alt+Tab

settings.help: While the list is up, typing letters filters it (hold Alt, press Tab, then type). Letters are only taken while Alt is held, and never replace a bind of your own.
settings.label: Type to search

settings.help: Also match initials (gc finds Google Chrome) and letters in order inside a word (chrm finds chrome). These matches come after the plain ones.
settings.label: Fuzzy search

settings.help: 0 (the default) keeps the usual way: releasing Alt picks. From 1 to 60: once you have typed a search, releasing Alt no longer picks. The list stays open this many seconds after your last key and takes the keyboard, so any character can be typed. Return picks, Escape clears the search and then closes, a click outside the list closes it, and when the time runs out it closes without picking.
settings.label: Keep the list open after typing

settings.help: Window classes, comma separated (for example: pavucontrol, steam). Case does not matter.
settings.label: Never list these apps

settings.help: The list is plain and light. Cards show a picture of each window.
settings.label: Style

settings.help: Snapshot takes one picture of each window when the cards open and costs almost nothing. Live keeps them updating and uses noticeable CPU with many windows.
settings.label: Thumbnails (cards)

settings.help: Window classes, comma separated, that are never captured into a picture (a password manager, a bank, a private window). Cards and the peek strip show the app icon instead. Applies to Snapshot and Live alike.
settings.label: Never take a picture of these apps

settings.help: A quick tap flips between your last two windows with no list. 0 shows the list at once.
settings.label: Delay before the list shows

settings.help: Auto draws no outline when you turned window borders off.
settings.label: Outline

settings.help: Type the folder name of an installed icon theme, such as Papirus, to prefer its icons. Empty uses whichever installed theme the scan finds first. An app the theme has no icon for still gets one from the others.
settings.label: Icon theme

settings.help: Type the folder name of an icon pack in ~/.config/omahop/packs, such as omahop-sample. Its icons come first; an app the pack has no icon for keeps its usual one. Empty uses no pack. A pack you made yourself or copied from someone: see docs/icon-packs.md for the format. Applies at once.
settings.label: Icon pack

settings.help: Show close and minimize buttons on the row or card under the pointer. Delete (with Alt held) closes the picked window either way.
settings.label: Close and minimize buttons

settings.help: A slim row of your running apps. Hover an app to see a picture of each of its windows; click to go to one. Off by default: nothing is added to your desktop unless you turn it on.
settings.label: Peek strip

names.edge: Show when the pointer touches the screen edge

settings.help: Auto picks an edge that is not the dock's and not the bar's, so nothing competes or covers the bar.
settings.label: Edge

settings.help: Fragments, comma separated (for example: picture in picture). Case does not matter.
settings.label: Never list windows whose title contains

settings.help: Window classes, comma separated. Their windows come before all others.
settings.label: List these apps first

settings.help: When the focused window is fullscreen (a game, a remote desktop, a virtual machine), Alt+Tab is left to it and works as Omarchy has it.
settings.label: Step aside for fullscreen apps

settings.help: Window classes, comma separated, for which Alt+Tab is always left alone, whatever their state.
settings.label: Step aside for these apps

settings.help: A second shortcut that lists only the windows of the app you are in, like Cmd+backtick on a Mac. It must start with the key to hold (for example ALT + GRAVE, or SUPER + GRAVE when that key is Super). Leave it empty to turn it off. Applies after a Hyprland reload; a chord you already use is never taken.
settings.label: Same-app shortcut

settings.help: While the list is up and nothing is typed yet, a hint key jumps straight to a window. Any other key still types into the search.
settings.label: Quick jump keys

names.numbers: Number keys (1 to 9, with the key held)

settings.help: Pairs of letter and app class, comma separated, for example: c=google-chrome, t=kitty. Used when Quick jump keys is App letters.
settings.label: App letters

settings.help: Pairs of key and action, comma separated, for example: q=close, m=minimize. While the list is up and nothing is typed yet, that key acts on the selected window and the selection moves to the next row; once you have typed a letter, every key types. Actions: close, minimize. Empty (the default) turns it off. A key a hint already uses is left to the hint.
settings.label: Quit and minimize keys
